title: India's Census 2027 Will Count Caste for First Time Since 1931
excerpt: The world's most populous nation prepares for its first population census since 2011, with a historic caste enumeration that could reshape welfare policy, parliamentary representation, and the political landscape.
body:
• India will conduct Census 2027 in two phases — houselisting begins October 1, 2026 in snow-bound regions, with full population enumeration starting March 1, 2027 across the rest of the country.
  • For the first time since 1931 under British colonial rule, the census will include a full caste enumeration, recording individual castes alongside demographic indicators.
  • This will be India's first fully digital census, deploying an estimated 3.4 million enumerators using mobile apps and a self-enumeration portal in 16 languages.
  • The data will inform future parliamentary delimitation exercises and the implementation of women's reservation in legislative bodies under the 84th Constitutional Amendment.

India is preparing for a census that will do more than count heads. When enumerators fan out across the country for Census 2027, they will record something no Indian government has officially measured since the British Raj: the caste identity of every citizen.

The Ministry of Home Affairs confirmed that Population Census 2027 will be conducted in two phases, with caste enumeration included as part of the exercise. The reference date for the population count is 12 a.m. on March 1, 2027, for most of the country. For snow-bound areas — including Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand — the reference date falls earlier, on October 1, 2026, before winter sets in.

A 96-Year Gap in Caste Data

The last full caste census was conducted in 1931, during British colonial rule that ended with Indian independence in 1947. Since then, India's decennial censuses have recorded Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and religious denominations, but the broader caste spectrum — particularly the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) — has remained invisible in official datasets.

A Socio-Economic Caste Census was conducted in 2011-12, but the government never released its caste findings, citing data quality concerns. That exercise was also separate from the 2011 general census, which remains India's last completed population count.

The demand for a caste headcount has persisted since 1957 and has been a rallying point for opposition parties for decades. The decision to include caste data was approved at a government meeting headed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in May 2025, meeting a long-standing opposition demand.

Digital-First, at Unprecedented Scale

Census 2027 will be India's first fully digital census. An estimated 3.4 million enumerators and supervisors, along with 130,000 census officials, will use mobile applications and a self-enumeration portal available in 16 Indian languages.

Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a preparation review on June 15, emphasizing robust data security and a digital-first approach. The gazette notification for the census was officially published on June 16, 2025, under the provisions of the Census Act, 1948.

"It has been decided to conduct Population Census-2027 in two phases along with enumeration of castes."

— Ministry of Home Affairs statement

What Caste Data Will — and Won't — Show

The caste enumeration will list individual castes rather than grouping them into umbrella categories like OBCs. This raw catalogue approach is expected to produce granular data that could inform more targeted welfare policies, but it also raises concerns about how the numbers will be interpreted politically.

The government has indicated that the exercise will not alter existing reservation limits, which remain capped at 50% by Supreme Court precedent. However, detailed caste data will be critical for future parliamentary and state assembly delimitation exercises, as well as for implementing women's reservation in legislative bodies under the 84th Constitutional Amendment.

A Delayed but Critical Exercise

Census 2027 arrives after a six-year delay. Originally scheduled for 2021, the exercise was postponed indefinitely due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The gap has had cascading consequences: India's entire statistical system relies on census data for its sampling framework, and an outdated base has raised questions about the reliability of national surveys and economic estimates.

More than two-thirds of India's 1.4 billion people are estimated to be on the lower rungs of a millennia-old social hierarchy. For policymakers, researchers, and the communities seeking greater representation, Census 2027 represents a chance to finally put numbers to a social reality that has shaped Indian life for centuries.
image_caption: India's Census 2027 will deploy 3.4 million enumerators across the country in the first fully digital population count. The exercise marks the first official caste enumeration since 1931.
nri_angle: Census 2027 has direct implications for the Indian diaspora, as updated population data will inform electoral delimitation, OCI documentation policies, and the allocation of welfare resources that many NRIs help access for family members back home.
